deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the Hilbert-space part of Grothendieck's 1953 notes on 'opérateurs de Fredholm', which here means trace-class (nuclear) operators, and Hilbert–Schmidt operators. It is the Hilbert-space model for his theory of nuclear operators and topological tensor products.

(1) It completes Prop. 3: u: E→F is Fredholm (trace class) iff h = √(u*u) is. Take h compact positive with spectral decomposition h = Σ ρ_i ā_i⊗a_i, where (a_i) is orthonormal. Then ‖h‖_1 ≤ Σ ρ_i‖a_i‖² = Σ ρ_i. Together with the converse on the previous page this gives ‖u‖_1 = ‖h‖_1 = Σ ρ_i, i.e. formula (20).

(2) √(u*u) and √(uu*) have the same nonzero eigenvalues. Use the polar decomposition u = Uh, with U isometric on the span of the a_i. Set b_i = U a_i, an orthonormal family in F. Then u = Σ ρ_i ā_i⊗b_i and u* = Σ ρ_i b̄_i⊗a_i. Hence uu* = Σ ρ_i² b̄_i⊗b_i and √(uu*) = Σ ρ_i b̄_i⊗b_i.

(3) Corollary 1 (Schmidt / singular value decomposition): the trace-class operators are exactly the u = Σ ρ_i ā_i⊗b_i with (a_i), (b_i) orthonormal and (ρ_i) ∈ ℓ¹. Moreover ‖u‖_1 = Σ ρ_i.

(4) The map Ē'⊗̂E → L(E) is injective, so the trace is well defined on trace-class operators of E. This gives (22): ‖u‖_1 = Tr√(u*u) = Tr√(uu*).

(5) Corollary 2 (trace duality): ‖u‖_1 = sup_{‖A‖≤1} |Tr(A∘u)| over A ∈ L(F,E). The reason given is that the dual of the projective tensor product is the space of bounded bilinear forms B(Ē',F) ≅ L(F,E).

(6) A remark that the notions of Fredholm and H.-S. operators are invariant under isomorphism (passage to the conjugate/dual space).

(7) Th. 4: if u ∈ L²(E,F) and v ∈ L²(F,G), then vu ∈ L¹(E,G) and ‖vu‖_1 ≤ ‖v‖_2‖u‖_2. This is the Hölder inequality for Schatten classes with p = q = 2, r = 1. It is proved on the next page via (22)/(23) and the Hilbert–Schmidt inner product (u,v) = Tr v*u.

The margin notes link ‖u‖_2 = √Tr(u*u) = √‖u*u‖_1 and the identification L¹(E,F) = Ē'⊗̂F.
errors: In the formula for U, the manuscript (as transcribed) writes U = Σ ρ_i ā_i⊗b_i. It should be U = Σ ā_i⊗b_i, the partial isometry without the weights ρ_i. With the ρ_i one gets u, not U.
√(u*u) and √(uu*) are written as elements of L(E,F). They lie in L(E) and L(F) respectively.
'Same eigenvalues' should read 'same nonzero eigenvalues (with multiplicity)'. The kernels can differ.
The equation number (20) on this page is inconsistent with (26) on the previous page.

ideas.what: Trace norm equals the sum of the eigenvalues of √(u*u), the singular values
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires (Mem. AMS 16, 1955), Hilbert-space section

ideas.what: u*u and uu* share nonzero spectra; singular value decomposition u = Σ ρ_i ā_i⊗b_i
ideas.modern_name: Schmidt decomposition / SVD of compact operators

ideas.what: Trace-class operators = Ē'⊗̂F, with injectivity of the canonical map and a well-defined trace
ideas.modern_name: Identification S_1 = projective tensor product of Hilbert spaces
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques; Résumé de la théorie métrique (1953/56)

ideas.what: Product of two Hilbert–Schmidt operators is trace class with ‖vu‖_1 ≤ ‖v‖_2‖u‖_2
ideas.modern_name: Hölder inequality for Schatten classes (p = q = 2)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but entirely standard textbook development of trace-class and Hilbert–Schmidt theory, already in Schatten–von Neumann and reproduced in Grothendieck's published 1955 memoir. There is no new result or unexplored connection.
transcription_corrections: 'op. orientiennes [?] de Fredholm' is likely 'op. de Fredholm et op. de H.-S. sont invariants dans l'isomorphisme ...'. Unclear; possibly refers to the isomorphism E ≅ Ē'.
'(En effet, le dual de E⊗̂F ...)' is more plausibly 'le dual de Ē'⊗̂F est B(Ē',F) = L(F,E)'.
Margin '(23)' near ‖u‖_2 = √Tr(u*u) is probably a separate formula label, (23) or (19)-related, in the margin addition.
